findings: subprocess exec without explicit shell parameter — runner.py calls asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*argv, ...) but does not explicitly pass shell=False. While create_subprocess_exec defaults to shell=False, explicit is better than implicit for security-critical code. Add shell=False to the call.

Evidence file memory consumption — final_gate_agent.py reads entire evidence files into memory when recomputing SHA-256 hashes. For very large evidence files (e.g., multi-MB test output logs), this could cause memory pressure. The code already chunks file reads at 8192 bytes, so this is a minor efficiency note rather than a blocking defect.

Hardcoded database allowlists — TRUSTED_TEST_HOSTS and TRUSTED_TEST_DATABASES are hardcoded frozensets in safety.py. There is no mechanism to override these via environment variables or configuration files. For development environments with custom database hostnames, this requires code modification. Consider adding optional environment variable overrides (e.g., TRUSTED_TEST_HOSTS_OVERRIDE) that extend the base allowlist.
